objective: Make gate health something Nightshift judges, records and repairs: planning audits a repository's gates against Nightshift's gate standard before ratification and the human decides each fix, and a run repairs a broken or flaky gate itself and records it as a decision, never re-planning. The authority is docs/programs/p15-gate-health.md.

stories.who: A developer bringing a repository to Nightshift
stories.problem: The gates fail in Nightshift's conditions for reasons nobody saw: installs folded into pre-hooks, two gates sharing a build folder, an undeclared Docker dependency. The first run finds out hours in and lands nothing.
stories.outcome: Planning tells them what has to be cleaned up before Nightshift can run reliably. They decide each fix once, and the first strand builds it.
words: suppose a super unhealthy piece of shit build starts using nightshift. nightshift should be able to say, umm, we need to get this cleaned up before i can reliably run
we can only do as good as their testing is setup

stories.who: The owner reviewing a run in the morning
stories.problem: A gate that breaks mid-run fails every job, retries climb to dearer models, and the only answer offered is to re-plan.
stories.outcome: The run repaired the gate itself, carried on, and recorded what it did as decisions they can review and reverse.
words: the fucking thing is designed to get the job done and record what happened so it can be REVIEWED. NOT replanned.

successCriteria.outcome: Planning a program on a repository with no healthy gate-health record runs the gates and the review against the gate standard, and turns each finding into a decision the human answers

`plan check` does not answer READY until the audit is complete: a healthy record matching the plan's gate fingerprint, or a repairing record whose findings are each answered by a decision, with a gate-health strand every other strand depends on
A later plan whose gate fingerprint is unchanged skips the audit; changing any gate-machinery file brings it back
When a gate-health strand lands, the project's record reads healthy for the new fingerprint
A red gate at the start of a run becomes the run's first job, a repair, and the strands start once it lands, locally and on a remote machine
A check that fails and then passes on the same commit lands the work, is recorded as flaky, does not climb the route, and opens a repair job no strand waits on
A repair job can change setup and gate commands, and the verifications after it lands use the new definition
Every repair job records a decision, and a repair that weakens a gate is stopped by examination unless its decision says why
The report and the Studio's Status tab show the gate audit, each repair with its decision, and each flake

constraints: docs/programs/p15-gate-health.md is the authority: its decisions and design hold, and a departure is recorded.
The mechanical audit stays deterministic; only the planning review and repair jobs use a model.
No run re-plans or re-ratifies: a repair is a run decision, reviewed afterwards.
The gate-health record is written only by Nightshift commands and the engine, never by an agent's file edit.
Every existing suite stays green, on Linux and Windows; no suite is carved out.
outOfScope: Repairing a repository's gates outside a program
Changing how a strand cuts, routes or examines its own jobs
Backfilling gate-health records for projects already planned
Deploying the API, the runner image or the Studio

forbiddenActions: deploy any stack or stage (cdk deploy, npm run deploy, image builds)
write to the dev or any hosted control plane outside the run's own records
read legacy history or the nightshift-archive repository (AGENTS.md greenfield boundary)

strands.name: The gate-health record and the planning audit

scope.summary: The gate-health record end to end, the gate standard, the planning audit, gates --record and plan check

acceptance: A project's gate-health record can be written by `nightshift gates {id} --record` and read back over the control plane, in every store
`plan check` enforces the audit as D-08 says, with every reason at once
The planning skill audits against the shipped gate standard and turns findings into decisions and a gate-health strand

strands.name: Repairs in the run

scope.summary: Flaky detection, repair jobs, repair-first starts, changing gate definitions, the setup reference, and the report and Studio surfaces

acceptance: A flaky check lands the work as flaky with a non-blocking repair job and a decision
A red base starts the run with a repair job first, locally and on the runner
A repair that changes a gate definition applies to later verifications, and every repair records a decision
The report and the Studio show gate health

decisions.question: When is the intelligent gate audit done?
options: At the start of every run
decisions.rationale: The owner: the human is initialising Nightshift and decides the fixes up front; they can wait. Findings become decisions, built by a gate-health strand every other strand depends on.

decisions.question: How is a completed audit remembered?
options: Per project, against a fingerprint of the gate machinery
decisions.leaning: Per project, against a fingerprint of the gate machinery
decisions.answer: Per project, against a fingerprint of the gate machinery
decisions.rationale: Fast without trading reliability: unchanged gates skip the audit.

decisions.question: What does a run do with a red gate at its start?
decisions.rationale: The owner: a run gets the job done and records what happened for review, never re-plans. One mechanical pass, no override flag.

decisions.question: What may a repair job change?
options: Anything, setup and gate commands included
decisions.leaning: Anything, setup and gate commands included
decisions.answer: Anything, setup and gate commands included
decisions.rationale: The owner: let it do whatever it needs. Every repair records a decision and is examined at high risk against weakening a gate.

decisions.question: Who defines a healthy gate?
decisions.rationale: The owner: Nightshift should have an opinion on gate standards.

decisions.question: What happens to a job whose failed check passes on a rerun?
options: Land it, record the flake, open a non-blocking repair
Hold it until the gate is repaired
decisions.leaning: Land it, record the flake, open a non-blocking repair
decisions.answer: Land it, record the flake, open a non-blocking repair
decisions.rationale: The owner: open a repair job, not on a blocking path, and log a decision for every repair.

decisions.question: Where does the gate-health record live?
decisions.rationale: Ratified 2026-10-06. Only a Nightshift command can write it; the Studio and a runner can read it.

decisions.question: How does plan check enforce the audit?
options: Healthy record for the fingerprint, or every finding answered with a gate-health strand
decisions.leaning: Healthy record for the fingerprint, or every finding answered with a gate-health strand
decisions.answer: Healthy record for the fingerprint, or every finding answered with a gate-health strand

decisions.question: Where is repair work shown?
options: The report and the Studio's Status tab
decisions.leaning: The report and the Studio's Status tab
decisions.answer: The report and the Studio's Status tab
decisions.rationale: Ratified 2026-10-06: the owner reviews what the run repaired.

decisions.question: What is a repair job's scope?
decisions.rationale: Ratified 2026-10-06. Conflicts go through the merge queue like any landing.

decisions.question: Is the program checkout the setup reference after a repair lands?
decisions.rationale: Ratified 2026-10-06: one real install per lockfile change, not one per worktree.
